components.institution_label: Paid Family Leave for Academic Appointees
components.description: ACA-50 paid family leave for family formation: up to 12 weeks at full salary for the birth or adoption of a child by the appointee or the appointee's spouse or domestic partner, after one year of service.
components.faculty_group_note: All full-time academic appointees with, at least, one year of service (10- and 12-month appointees; visiting, adjunct, part-time, post-doctoral and intermittent appointees not eligible; School of Medicine clinical faculty governed by a separate School of Medicine policy)

components.entitlement_note: V2: the policy provides the leave to eligible appointees ('Family leave provides eligible academic appointees with up to twelve weeks'; 'are eligible for family leave'); approval is routine through a request form (2012 VPFAA chart). The approval covers the arrangements, not whether there is a leave.
components.duration_note: 'up to twelve weeks'; 'paid leave periods will vary by need and circumstance and may extend across semesters'; semester breaks count in the leave period. The 12 weeks are shared with family-care leave (c9): leave_limits.
components.relief_note: Stated: 'An appointee should not be expected to perform duties while on leave, to make up time or work, or to be on call in clinical settings.' Absences of three weeks or less are arranged informally in the department.
components.time_window: must be concluded within six months of the birth of the child or the date on which the child is placed in the physical custody of the appointee
components.use_limit_note: 'Academic appointees may take family leave up to twice every five years'; 'The first week of any family leave begins the period for calculating both the twelve weeks and five-year eligibility period.'
components.return_obligation: must return to full-time service for at least one fall or spring semester between leaves (five months for non-teaching appointments)

notes: Governing documents on 2018-02-22: ACA-50 (last updated 10-06-2017), ACA-49 (1974), ACA-48 (2016). HR-05-20 (FMLA, last updated 10-24-2017) covers staff and temporary employees only. 2018_06_vpfaa_faculty_leaves_tenure_clock_chart_2012 is a 2012 VPFAA explanatory chart (captured 2015); it is guidance, partly stale (it states two years of service for paid family leave; ACA-50 changed this to one year from 2017-08-01). Used only for details consistent with the governing documents; conflicts flagged on c1 and c13.
2018_03_aca22_reappointment_probationary_period (ACA-22) and 2018_04_aca37_faculty_librarian_tenure (ACA-37) contain no leave, parental or tenure-clock-stop provision; recorded as not relevant.

Birth parent chain: pregnancy leave 6 weeks full pay (c2; c3, concurrent with it: half pay for the balance of the semester when medically required, containing c2; c4 discretionary extension to 9 half-pay weeks, in lieu of c3; c5 leave without pay after the paid periods; c6 general sick pay concurrent with c2) -> family-formation leave 12 weeks full salary (c1, also_available after c2; the 2012 chart: combined 18 weeks at full pay); FMLA 12 workweeks (c7) concurrent from the start of c2; childrearing leave without pay (c10, negotiated) unlinked.

Non-birth parent chain: family-formation leave 12 weeks (c1) and family-care leave (c9, care of the birth parent, U5) also_available, within the combined 12-week leave limit; FMLA 12 workweeks (c7) concurrent with them; childrearing leave without pay (c10, negotiated) unlinked.

c10 (childrearing leave without pay) is not linked to the paid leaves: ACA-49 makes it available under the leave-without-pay rules on agreed conditions, and no text places it before, after or alongside the pregnancy or family leave. ACA-50's flexibility clause mentions 'a combination of paid and unpaid leave' only within agreements for leaves spanning two semesters (c15).

c10 and c11 describe the same leave-without-pay mechanism: c10 is ACA-49's dedicated childrearing provision (C1), c11 the general ACA-48 policy (general_purpose, U1). Not linked; c11 counts in no figure.
